Name: Gamaliel, the Pharisee
Summary: Gamaliel was a Pharisee and honoured teacher of the law in Jerusalem, and Paul's teacher. Before the Sanhedrin he counselled restraint toward the apostles, arguing that if their work were of men it would fail, but if of God it could not be overthrown. He is distinct from Gamaliel son of Pedahzur of the wilderness generation.
KeyStory: Gamaliel told the council to leave the apostles alone, for if this work were of God, no man could overthrow it.
LifeLesson: Gamaliel's counsel still stands: works of men fail on their own, and works of God cannot be stopped by councils.
